source_en: Home from anatomy tutoring at the clinic. My mother expects me by six.
Back from school. I stayed late to redo an exam I did not do well on.
Picking up study materials from the district library before it closes.
Returning from the clinic. The volunteer program still runs, even now.
Home from studying with a classmate. My mother dislikes me being late.
Collecting textbooks the school released before they suspended lessons.
Returning to residence. There is nowhere else worth going now.
Back from the old clinic building. It is mostly empty. I study there.
Coming home. My mother will ask what I learned today. I want an answer.
Coming home from my job at the bakery. I left school last year.
Going home to my aunt. I have lived with her since I was small.
Skipped tutoring to see a film. My mother lets me choose.
Quit the volunteer ward. I want to be a hairdresser now.
Coming back from my office job at the post office.
Out late on purpose. My mother never asks where I have been.
Going home to my husband. We married last spring.
Going home to sleep. I gave up studying weeks ago.
Collecting my nurse's pension. I retired last year.
Here. I organized everything by date, in case that helps you.
I know the correct forms. I checked them twice before I left.
My mother says punctuality reflects character. I am not going to be late because of paperwork.
The line was longer yesterday. I timed it. This is already faster.
I brought everything you'll need. I don't like being asked twice.
I have a test tomorrow. I would like to be efficient, if that's possible.
My sister is waiting for me. Please, I've done everything correctly.
I don't understand why this takes longer every day. I follow every instruction.
I want to go home. I have already answered these questions the way they should be answered.
I checked everything. I think I checked everything. I don't remember checking it.
Something felt wrong on the way here. I couldn't say what.
I'm not usually like this. I don't know why my hands won't stay still.
I studied the wrong chapter, I think. I keep forgetting which one was assigned.
My mother would be disappointed if she saw me right now. I don't want her to see me right now.
I can hear my own heartbeat. That's not normal, is it. Is that normal.
I don't feel like myself. I don't know what that means, exactly.
Something under my skin doesn't feel like mine anymore. I should probably not have said that.
Please, just tell me if I did something wrong. I need to know if I did something wrong.
Thank you. I'll tell my mother it went well.
See, I told you I had everything in order.
I can still make it home before dark. Thank you.
Please tell my mother I'll be late. She worries when I don't come straight home.
I don't understand. I did everything right. Please, just tell them I did everything right.
My sister needs me. Please, someone has to tell her where I am.
I didn't even get to… tell her I tried…
I had a test tomorrow. I was going to pass it.
Tell my sister… I'm sorry I wasn't… better…
I keep a study schedule in my bag. I would like to keep it with me.
This isn't fair. I have never failed an inspection before.
Someone needs to tell my mother where I am. She will not handle this well.
I was going to become a doctor. I was going to be good at it.
My mother will say I brought this on myself. She says that about everything.
I never even got to finish studying today's chapter.
Where are you coming from?
The clinic. Anatomy tutoring, then the volunteer ward. It counts toward my application. I am expected home by six.
The clinic. The volunteer program still runs. They have us rolling bandages now. It is still practice.
The old clinic building. It is mostly empty. I study there. It is quieter than home.
The medical institute. I am in my third year there. Surgery, eventually.
Home. I am an only child, so it is quiet enough to study there all day.
The canteen at the textile factory. I work there now. I gave up medicine a long time ago.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
No. I sleep less than recommended, but that is from studying, not illness. I know the difference.
Headaches, behind the eyes. From reading by candle during the power cuts. It is not a symptom of anything.
I do not sleep much. My hands are cold. Circulation. I took my own pulse this morning. It is normal.
Nothing. I have not opened a textbook in weeks, so there is no eye strain to speak of.
No. My mother lets me rest whenever I like. She says grades do not matter.
I would not know. I faint at the sight of blood. I cannot even take my own pulse.
My mother expects me home by a certain hour. I would rather not test her patience.
I've read that the human body can survive remarkably specific traumas. It's fascinating, honestly.
I don't usually get nervous. I don't know why I'm nervous.
Do you think medical school takes checkpoint delays into account? I doubt it.
I've started noticing things about the body that I didn't used to notice. It's probably just my studies.
My teacher says I overthink everything. I think that's an unfair thing to say to a student who studies this hard.
I used to think I wanted to understand the body completely. Now I'm not sure I do.
My sister asked me if I was scared. I told her fear wasn't useful information.
I keep counting things. I don't know when I started doing that.
